name: AI Authors Studio (AAS)
author: martyettington

sections.description:
AI Authors Studio (AAS) gives authors a dedicated workspace inside WordPress for turning an idea into a structured manuscript.

Instead of starting from a blank editor, you can create projects, build outlines, draft chapters, organize front and back matter, and prepare working manuscript exports from one place.

✨ Included in this WordPress.org version

🗂️ Project-based book workspace — Create and manage writing projects inside WordPress.
🧭 Outline builder — Build, revise, and organize book outlines before or during drafting.
✍️ Chapter writing workspace — Draft your manuscript chapter by chapter in a structured environment.
🧱 Book organization tools — Manage front matter, back matter, and supporting book sections.
📄 TXT and DOCX import — Bring existing manuscript content into the workspace.
📤 TXT and DOCX export — Generate working manuscript files for editing, review, or publishing preparation.
🛠️ Publish workspace — Review formatting, layout, sections, and export settings in one place.
🤖 Optional OpenAI help — Add guided AI assistance for supported writing tasks after administrator setup.

The core workspace runs locally in WordPress. Optional AI help buttons stay off until a site administrator connects the plugin to the OpenAI API in AI Authors Studio (AAS) > AI Config. To use those AI buttons, the administrator must have an OpenAI API account or project with available billing or credits, create a secret API key, save that key in AI Config, and test the connection. ChatGPT subscriptions and OpenAI API usage are separate products.

This WordPress.org version does not require license keys or hosted subscription validation for the included local workspace tools.

✅ Good fit for

  • Authors planning a new book inside WordPress
  • Writers who want project structure beyond a blank editor
  • Users who want outlines, chapter drafting, and manuscript organization in one workspace
  • Site owners who want optional AI help without making AI required for the core workspace

🚀 Available Upgrades

AI Authors Studio is also available in expanded editions for authors who want more advanced writing tools, AI-assisted workflows, series planning, or collaboration.

⚡ AAS Pro

AAS Pro is designed for authors who want a deeper writing and revision workspace with more advanced build, publish, and AI-assisted tools.

Pro features include:

✍️ Advanced writing workspace tools
🧠 Leonardo and Editor Tools panels for guided writing support
📝 Chapter snapshots and book version tools
🔍 Book version comparison tools
🗃️ Storage and file-management tools for working project assets
🧭 Project outline templates and reusable outline-building tools
🛠️ Expanded publish workspace controls
📚 Readiness checklist and publishing-prep helpers
🔢 Page numbering and included-sections controls
📐 More detailed formatting and layout controls
🤖 Expanded AI-assisted drafting, revising, and publishing support

🏢 AAS Studio

AAS Studio is designed for authors, publishers, and power users who want the fullest AAS environment for multi-book workflows, collaboration, and more advanced production support.

Studio features include everything in Pro, plus:

📚 Full book series features
🔗 Multi-book planning and shared series asset tools
🤝 Collaboration tools for sharing projects, invitations, and replies
👥 Shared-with-me and incoming-invitation workflows
🖼️ AI-assisted front cover and back cover creation tools
🎨 Expanded organization tools for book packaging and publishing assets
🧰 More advanced workspace controls for larger writing systems
🚀 Premium AAS workflow features for more complex author projects

The WordPress.org plugin page focuses on the included plugin version. Pro and Studio are available separately as expanded editions of AI Authors Studio.

Separately, You can also get various productivity tools like the “Quick Start Pack” to help you start and organize your new book fast

External services

The core workspace runs locally in WordPress.

If an administrator enables the optional AI buttons, the plugin can send data to the OpenAI API configured by that administrator.

Service used when configured:
* Service: OpenAI API
* Service URL: https://platform.openai.com/
* Terms: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/
* Privacy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/

What is sent:
* The user’s AI request
* The current page context
* Limited project or chapter context needed to answer the request
* Model settings such as model name and max tokens

When it is sent:
* Only when an administrator tests the AI connection in AI Config
* Only when a logged-in user clicks one of the AI help buttons

Who controls the destination:
* The site administrator chooses the OpenAI API key and settings used by the site

This plugin does not require a paid AI service for normal workspace operation. The optional AI buttons require separate OpenAI API access.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP via Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open AI Authors Studio (AAS) in WordPress Admin and create or repair the master portal page.
  4. Open the portal page and create or import your first project.
  5. To enable the optional AI buttons, go to AI Authors Studio (AAS) > AI Config, add an OpenAI API key, save, and test the connection. The site administrator must have an OpenAI API account or project with available billing or credits. ChatGPT alone does not power these buttons.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require an API key?

No for the core workspace. Yes for the optional AI buttons: a site administrator needs an OpenAI API account or project with available billing or credits, and must save an OpenAI secret key in AI Config. The AI Config screen includes a setup guide for creating an OpenAI API key and testing the connection. ChatGPT subscriptions do not automatically include API usage.

Do users need their own OpenAI setup for the AI buttons?

Yes. The core workspace works without AI, but the optional AI buttons only work after a site administrator connects the plugin to the OpenAI API in AI Config. That requires an OpenAI Platform API account or project with billing or credits plus a saved API key. ChatGPT subscriptions do not automatically include API access for this plugin.

Which import and export formats are included in this build?

The bundled import and export tools in this build support TXT and DOCX only.

Does this build use license keys or subscription validation?

No. This plugin does not require license keys or hosted subscription validation.
sections.changelog:
2.18.77

  • Synced plugin header, portal version constant, and readme stable tag.
  • Refined the repository-facing description text and added screenshot caption stub text for five images.

2.18.47

  • Updated the package to use a five-character unique internal prefix (AIAAS) across classes, constants, hooks, options, transients, assets, and UI identifiers.
  • Removed plan gating from the repository build and made the local workspace operate as a fully enabled build.
  • Restricted bundled local import and export support to TXT and DOCX only, and removed unused extra-format files from the package.
  • Reworked remaining page-level inline scripts to use WordPress enqueue and inline-script APIs.
  • Updated the plugin header metadata and repository-facing author URL.

2.18.42

  • Continued WordPress.org cleanup on the free build.
  • Softened remaining Help-page wording so the free package reads more like a complete local workspace and less like a gated upgrade shell.
  • Shortened the shipped changelog to keep the readme more repository-facing while preserving the Info links requested for the free build.

2.18.32

  • Restored the Info submenu in the free build and added the public Info link back to the Plugins screen.
  • Fixed the readme short description warning by trimming the one-line description to fit WordPress.org parsing limits.
  • Updated the plugin author line to display By MKE with the http://mkettingtonbooks.com link.

2.18.31

  • Removed remaining off-site contact/info blocks from Help-page overview text and cleaned leftover internal HTML comments from portal output.

2.18.30

  • Tightened readme, installation, Help, and AI Config wording so the package more clearly explains that optional AI buttons require an OpenAI Platform API key, billing or credits, and a successful AI Config connection test.

2.18.15

  • Removed shipped reviewer-note artifacts and stopped the free build loader from bootstrapping premium module files.

2.18.13

  • Disabled series and collaboration action hooks in the repository free build and kept the package focused on the local book workspace.
